You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. If your child is 16-19, you normally still qualify if they stay in approved education or training; you can apply to continue for 20 weeks if a 16/17-year-old leaves education/training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Special rules cover: fostering (qualify unless the council pays towards accommodation/maintenance), adoption (claim as soon as the child comes to live with you; possible before adoption - contact the Child Benefit Office), looking after someone else's child (informal arrangements may qualify; may not if the council pays), living abroad, EU Settlement Scheme settled status (can claim) vs pre-settled status (claim if working above the primary threshold for 3 continuous months, looking for work for 91 days, sufficient resources, studying with sufficient resources, or family member of an EEA/Swiss national with a right to reside). You stop getting it if the child starts paid work 24+ hours/week and is no longer in approved education/training, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts certain benefits (e.g. ESA or Universal Credit). Two people cannot claim for the same child; HMRC decides if you can't agree. You may also be entitled to Guardian's Allowance.

HOW IT WORKS — (gov.uk/child-benefit): You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. There's no limit to the number of children you can claim for. By claiming you get: an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks), National Insurance credits counting towards your State Pension, and a National Insurance number for your child automatically before they turn 16. Even if you choose not to receive the payments, you should still claim to get the other advantages. You get National Insurance credits automatically if your child is under 12 (useful if you're not working or don't earn enough to pay NI); if you don't need them, your husband/wife/partner can apply to transfer the credits, or a different family member providing care can apply for Specified Adult Childcare credits. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

HOW TO CLAIM — 'Make a claim' (gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim): You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you; claims can be backdated up to 3 months from the claim date. Decide who should claim (only one person per child; the claimant gets the NI credits towards state pension; if you live together only one of you can claim the higher rate for the eldest child). If under 16, you can claim yourself or someone responsible can claim on your behalf. Claim online via the 'Start now' service (also to add a child to an existing claim), or by post or phone if you cannot apply online. Before you start you'll need: your child's birth or adoption certificate (if you have it), your bank/building society details, your National Insurance number (if you have one), and your partner's National Insurance number (if applicable). If you don't have the certificate you can still claim (takes longer; may be asked to send it as proof; if not sent when asked you may need to restart). You may also be able to manage someone else's Child Benefit claim.
